title: Probatorium results document
description: v5.4 schema for probatorium per-run results files. Additive over v4: every v4 field is still present, plus environment, benchmark_config, compile_options, latency_at_slo, hdr_histogram_b64, validation_results, soak_summary, (v5.2) per-(adapter, scenario) server resources, (v5.3) per-server cell_statuses recording cells that did not produce a real number (not_applicable / dnf) so they are not ranked as 0-RPS also-rans, and (v5.4) the 'suspect' status (cell ran but its loadgen error ratio blew the scenario's error budget — data kept, integrity flagged) plus per-server cell_run_statuses preserving the per-run outcome sequence so an OK rerun can never erase prior non-OK evidence. A v4 reader sees a strict superset of the fields it knows. Both the in-process runner and the cluster mage Bench path emit this single canonical shape.

schema_version.description: Schema generation tag. v5.x readers parse 4.x and 5.x; future readers will gate on the major version.

host_arch_pair.description: Lowercased <os>_<arch> tag (e.g. linux_amd64) — the canonical key for cross-host artifact catalogues.

kernel_sysctls_applied.description: Sorted list of key=value pairs the ansible role wrote before the run started.

rated_mode_p99_at_target_rps.description: Per-scenario merged-across-runs P99 latency, encoded as time.Duration (nanoseconds).

latency_at_slo.description: Outer key: scenario name. Inner key: SLO threshold in milliseconds. Inner value: max sustained RPS at which merged P99 stays below the SLO.

hdr_histogram_b64.description: Per-scenario merged-across-runs HdrHistogram (V2-compressed base64). Empty string allowed when a loadgen build did not emit a per-run histogram.

resources.description: Per-scenario server-side resource aggregate (RSS/CPU/GC/FD), keyed by scenario name. Optional (v5.2+); per-metric leaves are nullable so non-Go competitors expose RSS/CPU/FD only.

cell_statuses.description: Per-scenario outcome for cells this adapter did NOT produce a clean number for, keyed by scenario name (v5.3+). Value is 'not_applicable' (route/protocol unimplemented), 'dnf' (dial/port/crash/timeout) or 'suspect' (v5.4+: the cell completed but its loadgen error ratio blew the scenario's error budget). A not_applicable/dnf scenario is deliberately absent from saturation_mode_rps / latency_at_slo / hdr_histogram_b64 — it did not run, so it is never ranked as a 0-RPS row; a suspect scenario keeps its headline numbers next to the flag. 'ok' is documented as a value for completeness but never emitted (OK cells carry real numbers in the headline maps instead). Optional; omitted when every cell for this adapter ran. Older readers ignore the field.

cell_run_statuses.description: Per-scenario per-run outcome sequence in execution order (v5.4+), keyed by scenario name, emitted only when at least one run of the cell came back non-OK. Preserves the evidence of every run so an OK rerun can never erase a prior crash from the record. Optional; older readers ignore the field.

resourceStats.description: Server-side resource aggregate for one (adapter, scenario) cell (probatorium#154).

resourceSummary.description: Scalar headline of a cell's resource usage. Every metric is nullable: non-Go competitors leave goroutine/GC/heap null.

resourcePoint.description: One downsampled sample in a resourceStats.series. ts_unix is the observer's unix-second timestamp; metric leaves are nullable.
